effective_lease_rule: For ChatGPT workers, use the shorter of this rolling_lease_minutes and any longer lease advertised by an active review plan or translation epoch. Refresh only after durable checkpoint save.
released_claim_rule: A released claim is immediately takeover-eligible. The successor must atomically replace it using the current blob SHA, preserving the prior partial_result_path as handoff evidence before assigning a new claim_id.
partial_checkpoint_rule: Save a partial result after every checkpoint_every_decisions completed items or heartbeat_every_minutes, whichever comes first. A checkpoint is durability, not a stop condition: after saving, continue the same task or immediately select the next eligible unit while session budget remains.
productive_session_rule: Treat productive_target_minutes as the minimum voluntary-work target, not as a guaranteed wall-clock runtime. Before that target, do not voluntarily end merely because one batch, checkpoint, stage, validation step, or small subtask completed. Re-read live state and continue with the next safe eligible unit in the same priority lane.
early_stop_rule: Before productive_target_minutes, voluntary handoff is allowed only when the selected work and any immediately eligible continuation are complete, another worker owns the required non-expired serial claim, all repository paths required for the next safe step have actually been attempted and are unavailable, or a protocol/safety constraint makes further work invalid. Reaching a checkpoint, finishing one batch, stage transition, branch divergence, or one backend failure is not an early-stop reason.
continuation_rule: When a unit completes before stop_new_batch_after_minutes, immediately re-read live routing and claim/resume the next eligible unit at the same highest priority. Never idle merely to wait for handoff_start_minutes. If the current serial maintenance task completes early, advance orchestration and continue the next immediately runnable roadmap task in the same session when ownership and validation rules permit.
maintenance_heartbeat_rule: A maintenance lease refresh is valid only after NEW durable progress evidence has been persisted since the previous claim write. A time-only heartbeat that merely changes heartbeat_at/lease_expires_at is forbidden.
maintenance_progress_evidence_rule: Every maintenance claim refresh must record a changed progress_token plus progress_kind/progress_ref that identifies durable GitHub evidence, such as a new maintenance-branch head, a changed persistent task checkpoint, a newly completed validation/sync run, or an orchestration-stage transition. The same progress_token may never be used to extend a lease twice.
maintenance_no_progress_rule: If there is no new durable progress evidence, do not refresh the lease merely for time. Continue useful read-only/analysis/validation work while the existing lease is valid, or create a real durable checkpoint when appropriate. Lack of a heartbeat token is not itself a reason to end early before the productive target.
maintenance_finalizer_rule: Once domain content/research is complete, persist stage=ready_for_finalize. If enough session budget remains, the same owner should atomically transition its claim/state to stage=finalizing and continue bounded cleanup, integration, production sync/no-op proof, spot checks, and orchestration transition in the same session. Release for a fresh finalizer only near handoff, on a real ownership/capability blocker, or when the session cannot safely finish the next finalization step. Never restart domain inventory unless finalization produces concrete evidence that domain work is incomplete.
execution_backend_rule: Repository work is execution-backend independent. No external harness, plugin, shell, local container, MCP provider, or other backend is implicitly required. A failure of one backend is local to that capability and is not a task-level blocker while another repository read/write/execution path remains available.
backend_failure_fallback_rule: After a rate limit, EOF, DNS/network failure, unavailable shell/container, or transient tool error, preserve the task and claim, continue with available connected GitHub read/write capabilities, and use repository GitHub Actions/validation workflows for required execution evidence when the local runtime is unavailable. Continue safe work that does not depend on the failed path.
backend_failure_handoff_rule: Do not release or end a worker solely because one execution backend failed. Backend failure may justify exceptional handoff only at the normal handoff boundary or after every currently available repository path required for the next safe step has actually been attempted and is unavailable. Required acceptance tests may not be skipped when claiming completion.
session_end_rule: At handoff_start_minutes, stop starting broad new work, save the latest valid partial state, and hand off cleanly before session_minutes. If a small bounded step can safely complete inside the remaining budget, finish it first. Do not intentionally leave an active claim at session end.
throughput_rule: A worker may claim another batch/unit until stop_new_batch_after_minutes. Prefer continuing from released/expired partial work over untouched work when both have similar priority. Completing one unit early is a trigger to continue, not a reason to end the worker.
